summary: One property access must produce one callable and one invocation must return its captured property key; the Proxy trap and closure perform constant work per access and call.

optimality.argument: Answering one method access and invocation necessarily performs at least one access and returns one value, requiring Omega(1) work. The get trap creates one closure that directly returns the captured property key, establishing O(1) time per operation.

replacement_checks.evidence: A requested property must be intercepted and its call must return a value, which requires at least constant work.
The Proxy get trap allocates one zero-argument closure and that closure directly returns the captured property key without searching or pre-populating names.
Authored and Node-verified cases cover empty, ordinary, punctuation-heavy, spaced, prototype-like, and long property names.
